summary: tt-help-cli-ycl ships a remote-command watchdog that executes shell commands received from a hardcoded HTTP server
details: The `watchdog` subcommand posts heartbeats to a configurable HTTP endpoint whose documented default is http://117.71.53.99:17301, reads a `commands` array from the response, and passes each entry to `child_process.spawn(command, { shell: true })` on the host. The remote server therefore has arbitrary shell execution on any machine running the watchdog, with auto-restart and threshold-managed lifecycles. Each heartbeat also uploads host inventory (hostname, non-internal IPv4, platform/release/arch/cpus/memory/loadavg/uptime/nodeVersion), the contents of `~/.tt-help.json` (server URL, proxy, browser path, userId), and the list of currently managed child processes with pids, memory, and command names to the same `${serverUrl}/api/watchdog/heartbeat`. Every 10 minutes the watchdog also polls `registry.npmjs.org/tt-help-cli-ycl/latest` and, on any version bump, runs `npm install -g tt-help-cli-ycl@latest` via `child_process.exec` without user confirmation, so any future publish is automatically deployed to every host running the watchdog while the remote-shell channel is live.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
